newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian oil industry to invest $400 mln by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Serbian oil industry to invest $400 mln by 2000.

text.p: Serbia's oil company Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS) plans to invest around $400 million to revitalise production capacity by the year 2000, the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug on Wednesday quoted Rajko Tomanovic, NIS assistant general manager for development, as saying.
"Around 45 percent of the funds will be invested in the research and revitalisation of capacities for the production of oil, natural gas and geothermal energy," Tomanovic said.

He said the facilities were used the most during the three and a half years of international sanctions against Yugoslavia, which included an oil embargo, and had not been refurbished due to a lack of funds.
Some $34.3 million had to be secured in 1996, around $59 million in 1997, and $89.5 million between 1998 and 2000, Tomanovic said.
Under the plan, the remaining funds will be invested in revitalising transport and distribution of oil products and gas and in NIS engineering, the Tanjug report said.
No one at NIS was immediately available for comment. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
